name_en: Hassun — a mixed simmered dish of chicken, fish trim, and root vegetables
summary_ja: 安芸門徒の多い地域で、祭りや法事に魚屋を招いて出た「あら」と野菜を煮合わせたのが始まりという煮物。祝儀は器を朱に具を奇数に、不祝儀は黒の器に偶数と、盛り方に細かな決まりが伝わる。
summary_en: A simmered dish of chicken, fish trimmings, and root vegetables that began, it is said, when a fish seller was invited to cook for gatherings of Jodo Shinshu households. Custom dictates odd numbers of ingredients in a red bowl for celebrations, even numbers in black for funerals.

name_en: Wakegi no nuta — bunching onion dressed in sweet white miso and vinegar
summary_ja: くせがなく甘みのあるわけぎを白みそ、砂糖、酢であえた一皿。球根が次々分かれて増える性質から子宝の縁起物とされ、産地として知られる尾道を中心に桃の節句に食べられてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Mild, sweet bunching onion is dressed with white miso, sugar, and vinegar. Because its bulb splits and multiplies on its own, the vegetable is treated as a symbol of fertility, and around Onomichi—a well-known producer—the dish is said to appear at the Girls' Festival in spring.
source_title: わけぎのぬた 広島県

name_en: Nigome — a Jodo Shinshu memorial-day stew of azuki beans and vegetables
summary_ja: 大根やごぼうなど根菜を小豆とさいの目に切って煮る精進料理。親鸞聖人の命日「御逮夜」に作られ、肉や魚を使わず何度も煮返しながら3日間食べ継ぐと伝わる、安芸門徒の行事食。
summary_en: Root vegetables such as daikon and burdock are diced small and simmered with azuki beans in this meatless dish. Traditionally cooked for Otanya, the eve of the founder Shinran's memorial day, it is reheated and eaten over three days without any meat or fish, a custom of the region's Jodo Shinshu households.

name_en: Igisu dofu — a firm seaweed jelly set with soybean flour, no gelatin needed
summary_ja: イギスという赤い海藻を生大豆粉とともに煮溶かし、寒天のように自然に固める瀬戸内の一皿。酢みそやしょうが醤油であえ、盆や祭りに親戚が集まる際によく作られてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: A red seaweed called igisu is simmered with raw soybean flour until it sets on its own into a firm, agar-like jelly. Served with vinegared miso or ginger soy sauce, it was often made in Setouchi coastal towns when relatives gathered for Obon or local festivals.
source_title: イギス豆腐 広島県

name_en: Kuwai no amani — arrowhead tubers simmered sweet for New Year's
summary_ja: 鮮やかな藍色から「田んぼのサファイア」と呼ばれる青くわいを、だし汁と砂糖、くちなしの実で甘く煮る福山の一品。芽が伸びる姿から「芽が出る」縁起物として、おせちに欠かせないと伝わる。
summary_en: Blue arrowhead tubers—their deep indigo skin earning them the nickname "sapphire of the paddies"—are simmered sweet in dashi, sugar, and gardenia fruit for color. Because a sprout pushes visibly from the tuber, it is treated as a wish for new beginnings and served in New Year's osechi trays.
source_title: くわいの甘煮 広島県

name_en: Kure no nikujaga — meat-and-potato stew tied to the Imperial Navy's mess
summary_ja: メークインと牛肉、糸こんにゃく、玉ねぎを甘辛く煮る呉の一皿。イギリス留学中のビーフシチューを艦上食に仕立てようとした東郷平八郎の逸話にちなみ、旧海軍の料理として伝わる。
summary_en: Meakin potatoes, beef, shirataki noodles, and onion are simmered sweet and savory in this Kure dish. It traces back, by local account, to Admiral Togo Heihachiro's attempt to recreate the beef stew he ate while studying in Britain as a shipboard meal for the old Imperial Navy.
source_title: 呉の肉じゃが 広島県

name_en: Ohira — a broth-rich simmered dish served in a wide shallow bowl
summary_ja: 鶏肉と里芋、れんこんなどの根菜を乱切りにし、汁ごといただく大竹の煮物。大きく平たい椀に盛ることから名がつき、具の種類を奇数にして祭りや盆正月の縁起物として振る舞われてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Chicken and root vegetables such as taro and lotus root are cut into large chunks and simmered in a broth eaten right along with the dish, served in the wide, shallow bowl that gives it its name. An odd number of ingredients is kept for luck at festivals and New Year gatherings in Otake.

name_en: Nina — shredded daikon pan-simmered with fried tofu and dried sardine
summary_ja: 千切りにした大根を油揚げ、根深ねぎ、いりことしょうゆで炒り煮にする福山の日常菜。名に「煮」とあるが実際は炒め物に近く、食材の水分だけで仕上げるため手早く旨味が濃いと伝わる。
summary_en: Shredded daikon is pan-cooked with fried tofu, leek, and dried sardine in soy sauce, using only the moisture the vegetables release—a quick, everyday Fukuyama side dish. Despite the name meaning "simmered greens," it is closer to a stir-fry, prized by busy farm households for how fast it comes together.

name_en: Kaki zoni — New Year's mochi soup built on Hiroshima Bay oysters
summary_ja: 煮干しや昆布のすまし汁に丸もちと牡蠣、ぶりを入れる広島湾沿岸の雑煮。ぶりは年末に一尾さばいた残りを使う習慣があり、牡蠣は「福をかき寄せる」縁起物として正月に食されると伝わる。
summary_en: Round mochi, oyster, and yellowtail go into a clear broth of dried sardine and kelp in this New Year's soup from around Hiroshima Bay. Yellowtail traditionally comes from the leftover half of a fish sliced for sashimi at year's end, while the oyster's name puns on "raking in" good fortune.
